01-context.mmd: Shows lifter roles, planned training, profile insights, device alerts, export and the hosted account and sync boundaries.
Makes product responsibilities explicit without confusing TestFlight with a runtime workout service.
02-architecture.mmd: Connects local records and the sync outbox to Supabase, with separate device timers, ActivityKit and the system share sheet.
Explains why confirming a set is local and why the API still needs owner checks, idempotency and atomic writes.
03-navigation.mmd: Maps routine planning, preparation, set completion, rest, profile insights, export and reminder entry points.
Gives both coding models the same reachable screen flows; no story should exist only as an isolated service method.
04-data-model.mmd: Models routine prescriptions and independent workout snapshots with typed actuals, set states and existing synchronization records.
Keeps prescribed values separate from confirmed results and preserves historical records when routines change.
05-training-data.mmd: Persistent entity relationships for profile, catalog and device state
Models catalog provenance and region roles, owner goals and bodyweight, synced reminder preferences and device-local effects.
Separates persisted inputs from derived reports and keeps OS request IDs off the sync feed.
classes/01-ui-and-auth.mmd: Class model: controllers and account access
Defines each feature controller, auth gateway/session storage and bootstrap responsibilities. Routes/components delegate to these logical controllers.
Connects user actions to domain operations while keeping Supabase details out of screen code.
classes/02-domain.mmd: Class model: domain entities and services
Defines typed workout records, exercise/template/settings entities, validation, service operations and enum values.
Makes exercise-type rules, active/finished states, stable identity and template independence implementable rather than implicit.
classes/03-persistence-and-sync.mmd: Class model: repositories and backend handlers
Defines repository ports, SQLite adapters, transactions, sync coordination/gateway and logical PostgreSQL handlers.
Supplies the database-handler and API-controller responsibilities required by the assignment and supports failure recovery.
classes/04-presentation.mmd: Class model: conversion, progress and readability
Defines unit conversion, progress and accessibility presentation alongside muscle scoring, monthly reports, CSV export and device adapters.
Ensures graphs and plain summaries use the same numbers, and display conversion never corrupts originals.
classes/05-sync-records.mmd: Details operation snapshots, preserved conflicts, checkpoints, remote receipts and ordered change events.
Makes duplicate prevention, resumable pull and conflict preservation concrete types with durable fields.
sequence/SUP-01-auth-and-bootstrap.mmd: Shows first online sign-in, offline reopening of a known account, owner-partition initialization and sign-out safeguards.
Fills the selected specification's sign-in assumption without silently mixing account data or dropping pending work.
sequence/SUP-02-conflict-resolution.mmd: Shows presentation of preserved local/remote versions and explicit, validated resolution.
Resolves the source's undefined two-device-offline rule without a silent last-write-wins overwrite.
sequence/FW-01.mmd: FW-01: Start a workout, add exercises

As an experienced lifter, I want to start a workout and add exercises as I go, so that I can log in the order I actually train. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Specifies active-workout uniqueness and ordered exercise entry before logging.
sequence/FW-02.mmd: FW-02: Record a set with prefill

As an experienced lifter, I want to record a set by entering weight and reps, prefilled from my previous set, so that I can log between sets without losing rest time. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Separates the planned target from suggested and confirmed actuals.
sequence/FW-03.mmd: FW-03: Set form matches exercise type

As a home trainer, I want the set form to ask only for what applies to the exercise, so that I am not forced to enter a weight for push-ups or planks. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Prevents irrelevant weight/repetition fields from leaking into other exercise types.
sequence/FW-04.mmd: As a beginner lifter, I want to see what I did the last time I performed an exercise while I log it, so that I can choose today’s weight instead of guessing. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Defines which prior session is shown and how local corrections affect it.
sequence/FW-05.mmd: FW-05: Correct or remove a set or entry

As an experienced lifter, I want to correct or remove a set, or remove an entry, during a workout, so that one mistaken tap does not corrupt my history. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Preserves correction, confirmation and immediate undo behavior without renumbering corruption.
sequence/FW-06.mmd: As a returning lifter, I want to finish a workout and see a short, plain summary, so that I know it is saved and can read what I did. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Separates planned-session eligibility and confirmed skips from the ad hoc finish path.
sequence/FW-07.mmd: As a beginner lifter, I want my unfinished workout to still be there if I switch apps or my phone locks, so that an interruption does not cost me the session. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Restores plan snapshots, completion states and device-local rest after relaunch.
sequence/FW-08.mmd: FW-08: Record a workout on an earlier date

As a home trainer, I want to record a workout I already did by choosing an earlier date, so that I can catch up when I could not use my phone during the session. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Separates a training calendar date from timestamps so delayed logging is graphed correctly.
sequence/FW-09.mmd: As a home trainer, I want to log a workout when I have no connection and have it uploaded later, so that I never lose a session because of my signal. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Models the highest-risk cross-system path, including retries, receipts, conflicts and pull checkpoints.
sequence/FW-10.mmd: As a beginner lifter, I want to choose whether weights are shown in kg or lb, so that entries match the plates and machines I use. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Keeps account display preferences separate from immutable entered measurements.
sequence/FW-11.mmd: FW-11: Find an exercise; recent first

As a beginner lifter, I want to find an exercise by typing part of its name or filtering by muscle group, with recent ones first, so that I can add the right exercise without knowing its exact name. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Defines offline catalog search and stable exercise selection.
sequence/FW-12.mmd: As a home trainer, I want to create my own exercise with a name and a type, so that I can log home and unusual movements the library lacks. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Specifies private custom exercise creation, name conflicts and eventual type locking.
sequence/FW-13.mmd: FW-13: Rename or archive a custom exercise
As an experienced lifter, I want to rename or archive a custom exercise, so that I can tidy my library without losing history. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Keeps rename/archive changes attached to stable exercise identities and historical sets.
sequence/FW-14.mmd: As a returning lifter, I want to see a list of my finished workouts with dates, exercises and number of sets, so that I can quickly check when and what I trained. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Defines an accessible paged list with stable ordering and an honest empty state.
sequence/FW-15.mmd: As an experienced lifter, I want to open a past workout and see every exercise and set as recorded, so that I can plan a repeat or check what I did. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Provides complete, current records without forcing users through graphs.
sequence/FW-16.mmd: As an experienced lifter, I want to see every time I performed one exercise, with the sets from each session, so that I can follow one lift in numbers. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Makes exercise-level history reachable and robust to renaming/archiving.
sequence/FW-17.mmd: As a home trainer, I want to edit a finished workout, so that I can fix mistakes I notice later. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Carries all original validation rules into finished-record correction and derived views.
sequence/FW-18.mmd: As a home trainer, I want to delete a finished workout after confirming, so that accidental or test entries do not distort my history and graphs. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Explains both user-visible permanent deletion and internal synchronization tombstones.
sequence/FW-19.mmd: As a beginner lifter, I want to narrow my history to a date range or to one exercise, so that I can find a specific period or lift without scrolling. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Prevents date and exercise filters from accidentally replacing each other.
sequence/FW-20.mmd: As an experienced lifter, I want to see a graph of my total volume for one exercise over time, so that I can tell whether I am lifting more than before. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Ties exercise chart points directly to converted source sets and workout IDs.
sequence/FW-21.mmd: As an experienced lifter, I want to choose the period shown on a graph, so that I can compare recent weeks with the longer trend. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Keeps chart, table and explanation synchronized when period controls change.
sequence/FW-22.mmd: As a beginner lifter, I want to see my total volume per week across all weight-based exercises, so that I can tell whether I am training more overall. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Defines weekly bucketing, zero weeks and the zero-denominator comparison case.
sequence/FW-23.mmd: As a home trainer, I want to see my total reps per workout for a reps-only exercise, so that I can follow progress on bodyweight exercises. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Avoids assigning weighted volume or kilograms to reps-only exercises.
sequence/FW-24.mmd: FW-24: Select a point, open workout

As an experienced lifter, I want to select a point on a graph to see its date and value and open that workout, so that I can understand an unusually high or low session. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Preserves the link from a chart/table point to the actual contributing records.
sequence/FW-25.mmd: As a home trainer, I want to save the exercises of a finished workout as a named template, so that I can start my usual routine again without re-entering it. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Makes conversion of actual load and RIR into targets an explicit choice.
sequence/FW-26.mmd: As an experienced lifter, I want to start a workout from a template, so that its exercises are already in the workout when I begin. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Snapshots ordered targets while preserving legacy exercise-only routines.
sequence/FW-27.mmd: FW-27: Create and edit a template

As a beginner lifter, I want to create and edit a template by choosing exercises myself, so that I can set up my plan at home before going to the gym. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Applies routine changes only to future workouts.
sequence/FW-28.mmd: As an experienced lifter, I want to delete a template, so that I can retire routines I no longer use. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Ensures deleting a saved routine never deletes workouts started from it.
sequence/FW-29.mmd: As a returning lifter, I want to make the text larger, so that I can read my workouts and summaries without straining. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Makes large text a persistent app-wide presentation behavior.
sequence/FW-30.mmd: As a returning lifter, I want to see each weight with its equivalent in the other unit, so that I know how much to load when a gym’s plates use a different unit. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Uses one conversion/formatting path for every equivalent weight display.
sequence/FW-31.mmd: FW-31: Enter a set in either unit
As a returning lifter, I want to enter a set in either kg or lb, so that I can log what the plates say without converting. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Prevents a unit switch from silently reinterpreting a number without conversion.
sequence/TR-01-02-planned-training.mmd: TR-01 / TR-02: Plan a routine and complete working sets
Shows reusable targets, durable session snapshots, typed actuals, skip, undo and finish.
Makes the planned-row workflow and local confirmation explicit.
sequence/TR-03-13-rest-and-live-activity: TR-03 / TR-13: Rest countdown and iOS Lock Screen
Shows a device-local deadline, alert replacement, optional Live Activity, relaunch and cleanup.
Explains how rest continues under OS control when the app is suspended.
sequence/TR-04-05-preparation.mmd: TR-04 / TR-05: Warm-up and targeted mobility
Shows editable warm-up and mobility steps before or after working sets.
Preserves preparation in history and excludes it from working-set totals.
sequence/TR-06-07-catalog-and-muscles.mm: TR-06 / TR-07: Offline catalog, form guidance and muscle map
Shows a pinned catalog import, offline search, per-exercise form guidance and estimated muscle scores on a male or female anatomical figure.
Separates catalog roles from calculated set-equivalents, keeps exact values alongside colour, and gives each exercise an offline text equivalent of its photo demonstration.
sequence/TR-08-09-11-profile-progress.mm: TR-08 / TR-09 / TR-11: Reports, lift goals and optional bodyweight
Shows owner-scoped monthly comparisons, exact-variant lift goals and optional dated bodyweight readings.
Keeps goals and reports derived from confirmed work while preserving entered units.
sequence/TR-10-export.mmd: Shows date and file selection, owner-scoped local reads, CSV creation and the system share sheet.
Makes sharing and optional bodyweight selection explicit.
sequence/TR-12-reminders.mmd: Shows permission checks, local day/time scheduling, rotating messages and reconciliation after completion.
Separates user preferences from device request IDs and prevents duplicate reminders.
